leading_positions.synthesis: Six of the eight round-1 configurations name B049 (Katori, Ye) as the prize or its core. Shared: the magic-wavelength lattice idea is a distinct mechanism, uncertainties near 1e-18 are reproduced by several independent laboratories and compared across sites, and the two-name credit is compact. Not shared: how much weight Ye's contribution carries relative to Katori's concept (Olsson asks whether Katori alone would stand), whether the discovery content is new physics or instrument performance (Kroll's opening ranking and Lindroth's own caveat), and whether the 2005 and 2012 prizes overlap. Three of the six move to B049 from other opening first choices (Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson), and Pearce moved it to the centre of a two-part proposal. Within the B049 group, the second-ranked alternatives differ (B054, B024, B038, B044, B048, B045, B009, B011).

Eriksson alone prefers B048 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) as a single-part prize with a compound theory-plus-experiment citation. Mehlig and Pearce list it as an alternative and Danielsson as his first alternative. Shared across these members: the Z2 topological insulator physics is mature and independently replicated. Not shared: whether omitting Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (with Zhang deceased) and the 3D topological insulator contributors makes the credit defensible, and whether the 2016 topological prize makes it a continuation.

Danielsson alone prefers B024 (Luk, Kim, Wang) as a single-part prize. Pearce lists it as an alternative and Kroll as a second alternative after B054. Shared: the theta-13 measurement is mature, cross-checked and shaped later neutrino experiments. Not shared: whether it is distinct from the 2015 neutrino-oscillation prize and how three spokesperson names can represent Daya Bay, RENO and Double Chooz plus the accelerator appearance results; Danielsson himself rates it as the thinnest in breadth of support.

Pearce alone proposes a two-part prize, B049 plus a second part B047 (Halzen alone) for IceCube high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. The B049 part draws on the broad support above. The B047 part is explicitly held as droppable by its proponent. Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson each comment on it in their responses, and none lists B047 in their own configuration or alternatives; their stated concerns are the single-name credit for a very large collaboration and the more modest source identifications.

areas_of_agreement: B049 was the preferred configuration, or part of one, of six of eight members, and every member who commented on its evidence accepted that the lattice-clock performance is independently reproduced across laboratories.

Members who commented on the physics of B049 agree that the credit would need to be framed around the magic-wavelength concept and its realisation, not around precision metrology generally, and that this is the argument for distinctness from the 2005 and 2012 prizes.
No member challenges the experimental maturity of B049, B048 or B024; the disputes concern attribution, overlap with earlier prizes and weighting of discovery versus instrument.
Several members (Danielsson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce) say a single-name IceCube prize (B047) is hard to defend on the supplied credit; none opposes its scientific merit.

Several members (Eriksson, Lindroth, Olsson, Danielsson) raise the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize as a reason for caution about B038, and no member other than its original proponent now prefers it.
scientific_disputes: Discovery versus instrument: Danielsson, Kroll (at opening) and Lindroth note B049 is a measurement capability rather than a new phenomenon, while Johansson, Mehlig and Olsson treat the new regime (many neutral atoms at a magic wavelength) as a genuine discovery. Whether constants tests and geodesy have delivered enough to count as discoveries remains open.
Whether B024 is a distinct advance from the 2015 neutrino-oscillation prize (Danielsson argues yes while noting the overlap; Pearce, Kroll and Olsson raise it as an open question).

Whether B048 should be understood as a new state of matter distinct from the 2016 topological prize (Eriksson and Danielsson say yes) and how well edge conductance quantisation has been reproduced beyond the Molenkamp group (Eriksson cannot verify this).

Whether the IceCube source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, Galactic plane), which depend on one instrument, are mature enough alongside the secure diffuse flux (Pearce, Mehlig, Olsson, Kroll).
attribution_disputes: B049: Katori's priority for the proposal and first realisation versus Ye's record performance and many-body work (Olsson, Lindroth, Mehlig); other lattice-clock contributors named as outside the two names include Lemonde, Gill, Takamoto, Lisdat, Ludlow and Hong.
B048: the three credited names omit Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who proposed the HgTe realisation, and the 3D topological insulator contributors (Eriksson, Danielsson, Mehlig, Pearce).

B024: the three credited spokesperson names omit Double Chooz leadership and accelerator appearance results (Danielsson, Pearce, Olsson); Olsson cannot verify the credited trio from the historical record.
B047: Halzen as the sole name for a collaboration of hundreds, with the AMANDA lineage and other founders and spokespersons (Pearce, Kroll, Olsson, Lindroth, Mehlig).
B054, B045 and B038: five, four and four credited names respectively do not fit three places; Kroll, Olsson, Mehlig, Johansson and Eriksson cite this as a reason for not leading with them.
The B049 and B047 pairings differ in how many credited names they carry: two-name plus one-name pairing under Pearce, versus a single two-name part elsewhere.
maturity_disputes: Whether the pending redefinition of the SI second is relevant to B049 timing: Kroll and Lindroth do not lean on it, Pearce does not make it a precondition, Mehlig argues stability is shown by cross-continent comparisons, and Danielsson questions urgency.
Whether the scientific harvest of B049 (geodesy at scale, constants tests, dark-matter limits) is delivered or still prospective (Kroll, Lindroth).
Whether IceCube source identification has matured beyond a single instrument (Pearce, Kroll, Olsson).
No maturity concern was raised against B024 or B048 beyond the open question of how firmly HgTe edge-conductance quantisation has been reproduced outside the Molenkamp group (Eriksson).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (WACQT director, Chalmers) flags that B038 and B044 lie in or adjacent to his programme and that he would recuse or flag bias on B038, which he ranked first at opening; he has no tie to the B049 candidates.

Pearce (chair) works in PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur and flags field affinity for B047 and B024; he has no direct tie to IceCube, Daya Bay, RENO or lattice-clock groups and would accept recusal on B047.

Kroll records a distant mentoring connection to John Hall (2005 laureate, frequency-comb lineage, next to Ye's group at JILA), a research connection to rare-earth quantum memories relevant to B001 and B044, and a WACQT-related institutional overlap with Chalmers relevant to B038; he does not request recusal on B049.

Lindroth records close collaboration with Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and attosecond groups, and acquaintance with the precision atomic-structure community; none is a named candidate and no recusal is requested.

Eriksson reports that his Uppsala electronic-structure and magnetism work is adjacent to topological and moire materials (B048, B016) but has no listed collaboration with the credited names; he chaired the 2025 cycle and was an expert in 2023 and 2024.
Mehlig and Olsson record Chalmers colleagueship with Johansson without specific collaboration or recusal request; Danielsson reports no conflict.
questions_for_round2: For B049: is a two-name prize for Katori and Ye defensible, or does the committee judge that the invention and realisation belong to Katori alone, with Ye's performance and many-body work as follow-on execution? What would the citation say about the 2005 and 2012 prizes?

Is B049 a discovery-class result under the prize criteria, or an instrument and metrology achievement, and does the answer depend on any measured departure (constants drift, time dilation, geodesy) that has not yet appeared?

Can any member document a defensible one-to-three-person attribution for IceCube (B047) from the supplied material, or should B047 be dropped as a second part? Does the committee support a two-part prize in principle or a single-part prize?

Is B024 distinct enough from the 2015 neutrino-oscillation prize, and is the credit to Luk, Kim and Wang defensible given Double Chooz and accelerator appearance results? Danielsson, as proponent, should state which of these he treats as decisive.

For B048: should the citation be confined to the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators with the compound theory-plus-HgTe wording, and can Eriksson and Danielsson say whether the exclusion of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is acceptable?
If B049 is not carried, which of B048, B024, B054 or B044 is the committee's fallback, and does the allocation problem (more claimants than seats) rule out B054, B045 and B038 as fallbacks?
Does Johansson's recusal or bias flag on B038 and B044 change how those ballots should be weighed, and does the 2025 prize decide the question for B038?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows broad convergence on B049, with six of eight explicit preferences, alongside three distinct minority positions (B048, B024, and a B049 plus B047 pairing). Support for B049 is wide but several supporters moved from different opening first choices and carry open caveats on credit and overlap with earlier prizes. The recorded disagreements are mostly about attribution rather than scientific validity, and no member challenges the experimental maturity of the leading candidates. As chair I note that I proposed the second part, and my own field affinity for B047 and B024 is disclosed.
